cross_check.title: Cross-check with NASA's independent global record

ours.label: Our data (NASA POWER / MERRA-2), whole Earth, area weighted

arctic.label: Our data, Arctic only (north of 60 N)

antarctica.label: Our data, Antarctica only (south of 60 S)

reference.label: NASA GISTEMP v4 (stations and ships, a different method)

cross_check.plain: Our engine run on NASA's GISTEMP record finds +0.25 °C per decade from 2001 to 2025 (strong evidence, luck less than 0.1%). On our own data (NASA POWER, air 2 m above the ground) the whole Earth warms +0.17 °C per decade (moderate evidence, luck 4.6%), and +0.20 without Antarctica, where our data swings strongly (moderate evidence, luck 1.6%). The Arctic warms fastest, +0.35 °C per decade (strong evidence): the known pattern of Arctic amplification. Our global rate is a little lower than GISTEMP's: the two records measure slightly different things (air 2 m above the ground vs surface and sea temperature), and ours stays flat until about 2014 before rising.

false_alarms.title: How often the test cries wolf
false_alarms.method: Sen's slope + Mann-Kendall with effective sample size correction (decision D1)
false_alarms.plain: We made 20,000 fake 25-year series with Egypt's real noise and NO trend, and ran our real engine on them. It called 1.0% of them a trend (the target is about 5%; it is lower because in Egypt a warm year tends to be followed by a cooler one, which makes lucky trends rarer). With strong year-to-year resemblance it called 7.6%. The team compared 8 methods on 20,000 series before choosing this one (decision D1).

many_places.title: Testing many places at once
many_places.plain: Egypt has 323 grid cells. Testing each at p < 0.05 would show about 16 'trends' by pure luck even if nothing changed. Without correction 163 cells pass; after the false discovery rate correction 84 remain, and those are the ones the map calls proven.

checks.check: On world regions kept out of training, the model tells where a crop is grown from where it is not
checks.detail: AUC 0.90 averaged over 40 crops; 0.5 is guessing, 1 is perfect

checks.check: Trained without any Egyptian cell, it still ranks the crops Egypt grows (FAOSTAT) above those it does not
Sugarcane fits irrigated Aswan, where Egypt grows it
Cocoa, oil palm and rubber (humid tropics) do not fit Aswan even with irrigation
In Egypt's 247 dry cells (under 50 mm of rain a year), rain alone fits almost no crop

checks.detail: 0.00 other crops per cell on rain only

limitations: Each grid cell is about 55 by 60 km: it describes a region, not one farm.
NASA POWER is a model built from satellites and weather stations (MERRA-2): very good on large scales, less exact for one valley or oasis.
25 years is enough to detect strong trends; small ones may stay 'not proven' until more years are measured.
Future views assume today's measured trend continues in a straight line. They are not forecasts and ignore irrigation changes, new crop varieties and soil.

Crop scores come from a model that learned where 40 crops are grown today (IFPRI MapSPAM 2020). Where a crop is grown also reflects markets, policy and water, not only climate. A score is how well the climate matches, not a yield and not the chance of a good harvest.

Irrigated scores assume water can be supplied; they do not show that water exists. Soil chemistry, salinity and water supply are not included, and NASA's soil wetness describes the natural land, not a watered field.

Rain only scores fade to 0 below 100 mm of rain a year (a documented rule, since farming on rain alone needs about 200 to 250 mm), so in Egypt only wheat and barley on the wettest north coast can reach 50 on rain alone. Near that limit the model is cautious: it may miss some real rain-fed crops. Olive and date palm are not separate crops in the crop maps and are not covered.
We never claim why something changes; we say a pattern is consistent with a cause.

Rain in this NASA POWER record jumps around 2015 in many places at once (across Egypt about 3 times higher after 2015). That looks like a change in how the record is made, so every rain trend carries a warning.
